notes: Original, individually written short-form transmissions; no permutations of reusable opening/closing sentence fragments.
Mongoose Traveller 2e grounded: in-system radio is local; interstellar news arrives by ships/courier packets; jump-space isolation is absolute.
Rows with when.party=[inJump] are PRIVATE ONBOARD recordings/logs, not external radio broadcasts. They must not appear in a public scanner feed.
UWP condition keys, category names, established voice values and template placeholders preserved for drop-in use.
World conditions describe plausible local events and voices, not guaranteed setting rules. News items are fictional seed events.
Trade codes, travel zones, population, port class, bases and environment are narrative constraints. Conditions with open-ended numeric min retain original semantics.
Distress rows retain weight 0.2 for rare appearance; additionally enforce an application-level per-session cooldown if possible.
A few nonhuman speakers use distinctive pragmatic English instead of random mystical riddles.

lines.text: {ship}, squawk received. Stay outside the departure track. You'll get a vector.
No, captain, a flight plan is not a clearance. Hold where you are.
{port} approach. Traffic separation is in effect; the lane on your display is the one we mean.
Freighter on the inner track, we need your actual mass, not the filed estimate.
{ship}, reduce your acceleration. You're closing faster than the tug can match.
Inbound traffic, a tanker is crossing the corridor. Stop trying to make up time.
{ship}, you're cleared for the assigned approach. Don't chase the shuttle ahead of you.
Approach to cargo seven: your departure is delayed. The dock crew has someone inside your aft service hatch.
All hands on the outer corridor, expect a short hold. We have debris from a bad separation.
{ship}, your transponder is showing two hulls. Switch to backup and call again.
Flight operations at {port}. Whoever just dumped coolant across lane four, stay on frequency.
{ship}, we have your visual. Your port running light doesn't match your reported heading.
Negative, the docking collar is not certified until the pressure check clears. That's not negotiable.
Traffic from the deep-side marker, we see your drive plume. Give us your identifier before you turn.
{ship}, correction: bay twelve is closed. Twelve. I know what your ticket says.
{port} control. Two in the pattern, one departing. Take a number and leave room.
{ship}, you keep dropping off radar. Hold the heading and talk to me.
Inbound lighter, your turn is after the ore boat. He's heavy and he can't hurry.
That berth is occupied. If somebody sold it to you, take it up with them after landing.
{ship}, your ETA moved up nine minutes. Did you increase thrust without telling us?
Stand by for pad assignment. Somebody left a fuel hose across three.
{port} tower. Maintain current vector; the survey launch has right of way.
Your manifest is not a transponder code. Give me the code.
{ship}, don't use the west approach today. They're lifting a crane through the flightpath.
Copy your emergency reserve. You'll be first down when the tanker clears.
All pilots: portside docking cameras are out. Use your own eyes.
{ship}, the highport is not accepting unscheduled cargo. Confirm you intend to land planetside.
{port} field. We've got one working pad. Make this a tidy approach.
{ship}, come left a touch. A touch, not a course change.
You see the painted circle? That's the pad. Everything beyond it belongs to the fuel company.
Ground to the incoming scout. Nobody told us you were bringing passengers. How many?
{ship}, hold for the loader. He has no radio and limited sense.
Your approach is good. Watch the crosswind below the hangar roof.
Negative on the second berth. The tractor's dead in the middle of it.
{port} to descending traffic. If the red lamp is still on, you do not land.
You can have refuelling or repairs today. The crew isn't big enough for both.
{ship}, confirm gear down. From here it looks like you're keeping your options open.
That's not a ground guide waving you in. That's the mechanic telling you to go around.
{port} control. Two minutes. We're getting livestock off the apron.
We have the rescue cart standing by, captain. Say whether you need it.
Inbound, take the south side. There's a hole in the north blastwall.
{ship}, your heat signature says you're still burning. We need a quiet drive on final.
{port} on common. Who's asking for a landing? Say it again, slower.
There's a clear patch beside the big fuel tank. Stay away from the small one.
{ship}, you can set down when the truck moves. Yes, that's our entire traffic plan.
Pad lights are out. There's a hand beacon at the western end.
Ground here. We don't have a tug. If you can't taxi yourself, say so now.
The first pad has a soft corner. We painted it, but the paint keeps leaving.
{port} field. Your cargo is fine. Your exhaust is pointed at the clinic.
Inbound freighter, mind the power line beyond the berm. It isn't on your charts.
{ship}, we'll read you a wind check if the sensor behaves. Otherwise use the sock.
We're digging out pad two. Use one if it isn't occupied.
No tower after local sundown. Call your landing on common and keep the lamps on.
{ship}, you've landed here before. Stop asking whether the fence has moved.
That flare is the signal. It isn't a distress call.
{port} to the pilot circling us: there is no second runway.
I need you two ships to sort out who goes first. And do it on another frequency.
This is the field radio at {port}. Give me a minute; I've got gloves on.
If you're the ship overhead, the pad is the concrete bit. The rest is mud.
{ship}, no clearance required. There's nobody licensed to give you one.
The beacon's intermittent. It works when the generator does.
We can sell you fuel tomorrow. We can sell you coffee now.
Look for the yellow shed. Don't put your ship behind it; the roof comes off.
{ship}, we're not equipped for that kind of repair. I can give you a mechanic's name.
There are children near the fence. Keep the drive cold until they're clear.
No landing fee today. The payment terminal died with the last storm.
We heard you the first time. The receiver's good. The transmitter's not.
{port}, answering. You can land. We don't have a crane if you can't get back up.
No, we haven't got weather radar. We have weather.
The field's closed for a burial. You can wait until morning or land outside town.
Your navigation lights are the brightest things we've seen all week. Turn them down on approach.
No, that's not a hangar. That's the school.
Uncontrolled approach to {world}, this is a free trader descending from high orbit. Any surface traffic, answer.
Last ship out of {world} left a landing marker by the ridge. Can't tell if it's still there.
Calling all vessels near {world}. I'm on the north approach, low thrust. Please acknowledge.
No transponder traffic on this side of {world}. That doesn't mean there's nothing down there.
If you're using the old strip on {world}, check the western end. We found wreckage there.
Unknown surface transmitter, your beacon is leading ships into the mountains. Identify yourself.
{ship} making a blind approach at {world}. Surface frequency monitoring. One pass before descent.
Anyone at {world} operating a loader? It's on the pad, powered up, and moving by itself.
There's no traffic service here. Make your own separation and leave room for a bad pilot.
Unidentified hull near {world}, you're in our descent path. Please show a light or move.
Calling the old mining station on {world}. We have medical supplies. Is anyone awake?
No ground reply from {world}. We'll put down at the old survey grid and report from there.
Uncontrolled field, {world}. We have a shuttle coming up beneath us. Whoever owns it, call in.
Surface relay at {world} appears abandoned. Do not rely on the published approach frequency.
Clear the landing area before you tell us it's clear. We're not coming around twice.
{port} highport, bay rotation in progress. No manual approaches until the arms stop.
{ship}, don't match the station's lights. Match the velocity vector we sent you.
Tug three, your client's drifting. Say if you need another unit.
Shuttle twelve, stop transmitting on the cargo frequency. Your passengers don't have priority.
{ship}, your docking solution is good. Cut thrust at the mark; the tug takes it from there.
We have a pressure fault in the visitor wing. All passenger shuttles hold dockside.
{port} highport. No EVA across the arrivals corridor. We shouldn't have to say that.
Inbound courier, you're early. The berth is still full of somebody else's freight.
Yes, we know the berth number changed. Your computer knows too. Read the update.
All cargo boats: radiation exclusion around the naval hull remains active. Keep your distance.
Contact control before separating from the station. We have three maintenance craft outside.
{ship}, your bay door is opening into a service gantry. Stop it now.
No, captain, the station is not moving to meet you.
A passenger's loose in the shuttle staging area. Transports hold their doors until security clears it.
Docking coordinator to tug five: I said aft, not beneath. Beneath is worse.
{port} orbital control. Shuttle service is down to one hull. Expect delays.
{ship}, your allocated berth is on the far side. Don't shortcut through the repair yard.
Station to departing launch. The inner airlock still shows a person in it.
We can take your cargo aboard. We cannot unload it until the hoist is fixed.
Inbound, watch the unlit structure on the station's sunward side.
That isn't a docking beacon. That's a welding lamp. Follow the chart.
{ship}, reduce closing speed. Two meters a second is plenty when the collar is bent.
Surface shuttle, confirm all personnel are accounted for before you undock.
The fuel barge has a leak. Keep ignition sources clear of the aft service platform.
All traffic, maintenance is moving a disabled launch across the docking approach.
Control to the survey ship, we are not a repair station. We can give you somewhere to wait.
{ship}, we got your request. A customs inspector will meet you at the airlock.
{port} approach. Naval departure at the inner marker. Civilian traffic hold outside it.
{ship}, that's a restricted berth. Turn away now; they'll call you themselves if they want you.
Military priority inbound. No, we don't have a revised release time.
Port authority to base operations: your pinnace is sitting on a civilian approach vector again.
{ship}, copy that you saw the patrol. Do not attempt to follow it.
Port control. Three naval small craft clearing the departure lane. Stand by.
The base has put a security hold on your docking request. We don't know why.
We've been instructed to keep the corridor open. Yes, that instruction applies to you.
{port} control. Scout Service tender crossing your approach. Maintain vector.
Scout launch to tower, we're bringing back a sick crewman. Request the nearest working berth.
{ship}, the survey boat has priority. They'll be gone when they're gone.
The Scout base has asked for clear air around its antenna farm. Don't overfly it.
Approach, that's the third time you've asked about the scout's cargo. Our answer hasn't changed.
The survey crew is flying without exterior lights. They've been advised. Give them distance.
{port} traffic. There's a Scout launch coming in low and fast. Stay outside the pattern.
{ship}, your reserved pad is now medical priority. We're finding you another patch of concrete.
Base traffic to field: one modular cutter outbound. It needs the whole lane.
We've lost the survey pilot's voice but still have telemetry. Leave the approach clear.
{ship}, that battered launch belongs to the scouts. It'll land when it's ready.
Ground says the base is moving a sealed tank across the apron. Nobody has told ground what's inside.
{port} field. One scout lander is coming down with a stuck gear. Watch the south end.
Negative, no civilian refuel at the base. Please stop asking the base.
Survey section has a drone recoverable in the lane. All landings suspend one minute.
The base is operating tonight. Keep your beacon on or expect to be challenged.
{ship}, we didn't tell you to follow the scout. We told you to follow the scout's previous heading.
Base to civilian pilot, your transponder is visible. Your ship is not. Verify coordinates.
Inbound personnel shuttle, you'll park by the ambulance. Make sure it can get out.
{port} ground. The Scout Service is testing a drive. Expect interference, not permission to improvise.
Everybody east of the base, clear the pattern. No, I don't have details.
{ship}, send the cargo list now. If it matches the crates, this will be quick.
Customs to {ship}. Is your captain awake or do I need the mate?
No, I'm not interested in your engine hours. How many passengers did you bring?
One signed copy, please. I don't need a history of the company.
You can leave the ship sealed while we look at the papers.
{ship}, does anybody aboard know what the word 'declared' means?
Cargo accepted. The passenger list has an extra name. Who's Daran?
All right, your hold is clear. Next time make the boxes agree with the manifest.
We're not inspecting the groceries. We're counting the containers.
This is customs. The hatch you want is marked arrivals. The one you're using is marked fuel.
{ship}, I can read your cargo code. Tell me what it actually is.
Look, just put a number on the sample crate and bring it to the window.
We need a contact address ashore. 'Probably a hotel' isn't one.
Your ship is fine. Your paperwork arrived a week after you did.
There's no queue at the moment. There will be if we keep talking.
Crew member four isn't on your roster. Either amend the roster or explain why.
I don't care who packed it. I need somebody to sign for it.
{ship}, this is a routine entry check. Stop whispering on the open channel.
Was this cargo sealed when you took possession? It's a yes-or-no question.
The manifest says agricultural machinery. Why is it refrigerated?
You said six containers on approach. I'm looking at seven.
No, you're not in trouble. You're holding up twelve ships who aren't in trouble either.
Is there a doctor aboard? Your passenger declaration says 'quarantine observation' and nothing else.
If you have nothing to declare, say that. Don't fill the silence.
Next ship. Captain's name, registry, last port.
{ship}, customs. We'll take your amended manifest, not your explanation of the first one.
Passenger count changed between the outer marker and docking. Explain.
Your bonded cargo remains aboard until the inspector gets here.
You've filed the wrong port of origin. The computer won't accept it. Neither will I.
I have your papers. I do not have your animal declaration.
{ship}, send the crew documents as individual files. Not a photograph of the table.
That's a commercial sample, then? Why are there forty of them?
No one is impounding your ship. The declaration is incomplete.
We found the seal broken on container nine. Captain, I need you present.
You may hire local stevedores after the hold is released. Not before.
If you're transshipping, I need the destination manifest, not just the bill of lading.
The cargo broker has signed. The ship's master hasn't.
You can dispute the fee at the office. You can't dispute it over approach.
The return goods go on a separate form. I know they came in the same crate.
{ship}, we require an actual signature. Your autopilot's acknowledgement doesn't count.
I have three ships claiming the same consignment. Sit tight while I ask the shipper.
Captain, that permit expired before you left your last system.
No, the clerk won't come aboard to count loose bolts. Bag them and submit a quantity.
Manifest checked. Await final clearance before opening the freight lock.
The cargo says machinery but your loading plan says live biologicals. Which file is correct?
{ship}, port office wants a copy of the manifest. Port office is a shed beside the pump.
The local clerk is away until second watch. You can wait or leave your deposit with the harbourmaster.
Nobody's claiming the authority to stop you. We'd still like to know what you've brought.
Customs? On {world} it's one table and whoever remembered to bring the stamp.
If the town council signs this, the port office will honour it. That's the arrangement today.
They've changed the landing fee again. Customs has not changed the entry form.
Captain, three settlements claim this pad. Which one are you delivering to?
Please write the recipient's name legibly. Somebody has to walk the package across town.
Local entry is by declaration. And if you meet the man with the blue armband, he's not customs.
{ship}, company freight desk wants the bill of lading before local customs releases it.
Your cargo belongs to a different operating division. That is apparently our problem now.
The company stamp is valid. Your employee number is not.
We're going to need the original purchase order. Yes, even though we made the purchase.
You can clear the cargo with us; you need site access from personnel.
No, the unloading crew cannot accept a verbal change to a contract.
{ship}, I have no record of your employer authorising this visit.
Customs says clear. Corporate security has put a hold on the passenger group.
You are welcome to protest the assessment. There's a department for that.
{ship}, identify every person who crossed your airlock since the last port.
Remain docked. We're checking the departure warrants.
Who authorised your passenger to disembark? Give me a name.
Send the full hold inventory, including the empty stowage units.
We are boarding with two inspectors. Keep the main passage clear.
No, captain. We've moved beyond an amended manifest.
The ship's seal was broken on arrival. I need to know by whom.
Crew are to remain at their assigned muster points until called.
You've submitted two different names for the same traveller. Which is the legal one?
Customs to {ship}. We need the sealed sample, not a spectrograph reading of it.
That document was issued on another world. We need the current local entry endorsement.
Stand by. Immigration and cargo control are not the same office.
We're not discussing guilt. We're establishing custody of these containers.
Your transfer papers name a vessel that hasn't arrived.
{ship}, lower the boarding ramp. Leave the security gate closed.
Do not erase the cargo log. If it's wrong, we can record a correction.
You are not cleared to take on new freight until the outbound inspection.
A medical officer will review the passenger manifest. Nobody leaves before that happens.
We've got a discrepancy in your life-support consumables. Tell me where the additional load went.
Your ship's agent has left the building. You may wish to contact them.
I have two manifests, one from the broker and one from your purser. They disagree.
Captain, answer my question. Was the container opened during transit?
Security has requested the names of anyone with access to the freight controls.
Your papers aren't lost. They're under review, which is a different problem.
I didn't ask if the cargo was harmless. I asked if it was declared.
The inspector is wearing a recording unit. So am I. Please continue.
You will receive a written decision. I can't make it on this channel.
The entry officer has your signature and no corresponding identity record.
The declaration line for personal weapons is blank. That is not the same as 'none.'
The inspection is complete. Stay aboard until the release notice reaches your ship.
{ship}, your ramp stays shut until the inspection detail reaches the outer lock.
We have your names. Now transmit the biometric confirmation.
I am not authorised to tell you why clearance was delayed.
The passenger listed as 'crew guest' requires an independent entry record.
Captain, I need a direct answer from you, not your ship's computer.
The inspection team will attach their own seal. Do not remove it.
Your cargo is recorded. Your explanation is not required at this stage.
The officer in charge will contact you. I cannot put you through.
Who instructed your engineer to power down the recorder?
{ship}, acknowledge receipt of the detention order. That's all we need you to say.
We have an amended list. We still require the original.
Do not move the berth. The berth may not be moved. This is your third warning.
Your visitor permit covers the transfer corridor only. The rest of the port is not available to you.
State the names of all crew now. One at a time. Wait for acknowledgement.
No. 'Imperial citizen' is not an exemption from an entry inspection.
We have an unidentified container in the aft hold. Secure it and stay clear.
Captain, customs has placed a hold. There is no appeal over this frequency.
The individual you requested has no current release authorisation.
Yes, your ship is still on the departure board. No, that is not permission to depart.
Hold your crew at the inner lock. An officer is coming to speak to each of them.
{world} agricultural board has reopened the south loading sheds after the feed contamination scare. The destroyed stock will not be compensated.
Three harvest crews walked off the cooperative's fields this morning. Negotiations resume at dusk.
A delayed shipment of seed cultures has finally cleared the port. Growers have already begun rationing distribution.
The grain exchange says the first harvest estimate was overstated. Buyers are refusing to cancel contracts.
A fence dispute outside the capital has blocked the main produce route for a second day.
The irrigation authority denies that the new diversion has affected the downstream farms. Downstream farms disagree.
Port inspectors have rejected two refrigeration containers. Perishables crews are asking who pays for the lost cargo.
Agricultural freight is taking priority at the east gate until the crop is moved. Passenger transport is unaffected, for now.
Two prospecting teams in the {world} belt have registered claims to the same body. Arbitration begins when both crews return.
A mining cutter has reported structural damage after a drill charge fired early. All personnel are accounted for.
Local rock exchange suspended one ore certificate pending independent assay. Traders are still taking offers in the corridors.
The owners of a derelict processor have returned, fourteen years after the salvage notice was filed.
A miner reported an illegal tracking beacon attached to their ore sled. Investigation is ongoing.
Survey cartographers are disputing the classification of a newly logged carbonaceous body.
An oxygen shipment missed the outer mining camps yesterday. Contractors blame the tender schedule.
A union vote at the refinery will decide whether the next load of ore gets shipped at all.
Automatic signal from {world} reports the old survey station drawing power. No crew registry is active.
A merchant captain has challenged the accuracy of the published landing coordinates for {world}. The notice remains in place.
An abandoned communications buoy near {world} continues transmitting an incomplete maintenance request.
The latest navigation survey of {world} shows no verified habitation. That's the third survey to say so.
Port information for {world} has been marked unconfirmed following multiple unanswered approaches.
A cargo canister recovered off {world} bears a registry number that doesn't appear in the current database.
The northern caravan hasn't reached the {world} depot. A recovery team left before first light.
Desalination plant maintenance will reduce domestic water pressure in the western settlements.
An unlicensed water broker has been detained after selling the same tanker load to six customers.
The port road remains closed after shifting sand exposed an old fuel line.
Two cooling shelters are taking additional residents. The municipal office asks visitors not to use their emergency reserves.
Dust has interrupted the surface microwave link again. The city network is running on a reduced repeater.
Surveyors report a new sinkhole beneath the southern approach road. Heavy transports are being diverted.
{world} authorities have opened an inquiry into missing water-meter records from the last quarter.
Crews at the {world} coastal installation have isolated a leaking transfer manifold. No injuries are confirmed.
Environmental inspectors are looking into a discharge detected downstream of the floating refinery.
Transit across the primary fluid basin is suspended pending a hull survey of the public ferry.
An argument over pumping rights has halted construction at the southern reservoir complex.
The port's corrosion-monitoring station has gone offline for the second time this week.
A rescue craft from the outer platform returned with one passenger fewer than its departure list.
{world} horticultural authority has blocked imports of an offworld climbing vine after it escaped a test garden.
The parks department says the eastern preserve is closed to visitors. No reason has been entered on the public notice.
A dispute over heritage farmland will be heard by the district court on sixth-day.
Residents along the greenway are protesting plans to put a freight tram through the reserve.
The botanical academy confirmed the loss of two seed vault samples. Internal security is investigating.
Visitors are being asked not to feed the animals around the starport. The animals have apparently learned the shuttle timetable.
Transit police have reopened two stations after yesterday's crush at the interchange. The inquiry into the alarm continues.
The apartment tower evacuation has passed into its second shift. Temporary beds are being set up in the concourse.
{world} municipal grid is drawing on reserve power following failures in the lower districts.
A transport strike has stranded thousands of night workers. Private fares are now under review.
The regional hospital has asked for additional blood-plasma shipments. No public explanation has been given.
The city assembly recessed after an argument over a vote count. Recordings of the session have been requested.
The main port access corridor is open again, but freight drivers report delays well beyond the posted estimate.
Port residents have been asked to avoid the central plaza after a false evacuation notice caused injuries.
The {world} research council reports that last month's drive trials caused no permanent damage. Residents may submit repair claims anyway.
A prototype medical printer has been withdrawn after producing inconsistent implant batches.
The port is auctioning obsolete avionics tomorrow. Buyers are advised to bring compatible readers.
The systems institute has suspended publication of a new atmospheric model pending replication.
A demonstration of a self-assembling gantry was halted when the frame began dismantling the spectator barrier.
The licensing dispute over a starship sensor package has moved to civil court.
The local technical college is offering cash for examples of pre-standard computer cores.
An engineering firm says the batch recall affects power converters, not reactors. Independent tests are ongoing.
The outer access tunnel on {world} remains shut after the ice shifted against its supports.
A survey party reported missing heat shelters along the northern traverse.
Port crews have been ordered to check landing gear bays for trapped ice before launch.
An ice hauler carrying medical supplies has gone off its scheduled track. Searchers last heard it at the ridge beacon.
The geothermal pumps in settlement three are operating again after two days on backup.
The seasonal crossing has fractured. Surface travellers are being routed around the western shelf.
A power interruption stopped three {world} assembly lines overnight. Production supervisors expect a backlog.
Port labour representatives are meeting management over a disputed automated loading contract.
The refinery reported an unauthorised shutdown of its secondary furnace. Nobody has yet claimed responsibility.
A shipment of drive housings has failed stress inspection. Buyers have been notified privately.
Workers at the orbital yard have refused overtime until the last accident report is released.
The foundry says the airborne particulates above district six are within limits. Residents are asking whose limits.
Two industrial consortia are bidding for the same abandoned fabrication plant.
The station's automated night shift kept assembling units after a stop order. Inspectors are still counting them.
The single public clinic on {world} has reopened after repairs to its air scrubbers.
Settlement council elections are expected to go ahead despite the resignation of both candidates.
The school has requested an offworld teacher. The previous contract ended unexpectedly.
A damaged agricultural crawler is blocking the track between the port and the eastern settlement.
The local assembly has postponed its meeting because two members are aboard the same delayed ship.
A census officer has requested confirmation that the outlying research camp is still occupied.
The {world} machinists' guild has completed another replacement gear for the port's main hoist. Testing starts tomorrow.
Local authorities are investigating the sale of counterfeit generator parts to remote settlements.
The road from the field remains impassable to wheeled freight. Pack transport is available at additional cost.
The town foundry is hiring workers familiar with offworld equipment, provided they can work without spare parts.
The waterwheel at the municipal mill is operating again after repairs to its axle.
The customs office requests that visiting crews retain their own translation devices while ashore.
The {world} environmental bureau warns that a scheduled seal inspection may briefly interrupt access to habitat block four.
A contractor has admitted fault in last week's oxygen-credit overcharges. Refunds have not been scheduled.
Pressure doors at the public transit hub are operating manually pending a control-system review.
An unauthorised exterior camp has been found beyond the settlement's maintained life-support perimeter.
The food reclamation plant has rejected a shipment of contaminated feedstock.
The habitat authority is investigating repeated tampering with the exterior atmosphere sensors.
{world} merchants have petitioned for a regular freight slot. They say buying space one hold at a time is putting them out of business.
The credit union has extended its payment deadline for farms awaiting the next scheduled trader.
A visiting medical team has offered additional clinics if the town can provide rooms.
The local shipyard contract has been awarded to a firm with no permanent employees on {world}.
Two shops on the main street have combined their deliveries to meet minimum freight charges.
A residents' meeting voted to repair the old landing beacon instead of building a new market roof.
The {world} relief office has revised its food distribution schedule following complaints about missing households.
Workers at the municipal pumping station say two of its backup units were sold as scrap.
Unemployment claims have risen since the closure of the outer processing plant.
The town council has rejected another increase in port utility charges. Service operators are threatening cuts.
The medical clinic reports a shortage of sterilisation supplies and has asked ships to declare any available stock.
A crowd gathered outside the freight office demanding the whereabouts of a delayed relief shipment.
The {world} yacht registry reports a sharp increase in last-minute departures. Officials say there is no cause for concern.
An auction of inherited orbital property has been postponed while the estate's ownership records are examined.
Port authorities have closed a private hangar after a disagreement over unpaid maintenance fees.
A luxury liner has delayed its sailing over a missing passenger. It has not released the passenger's name.
The colonial museum has recovered an antique astrogation instrument reported stolen three decades ago.
Security staff at the exclusive upper concourse have been replaced without explanation.
Two pressure alarms in {world}'s residential network were traced to faulty maintenance reports.
The civic council has postponed an expansion of the underground market until the new seals are tested.
Exterior survey workers have requested additional suit lockers after the last decompression exercise.
A private shelter operator has been accused of charging for emergency air access.
An abandoned pressure dome outside the main settlement briefly came online during last night's system check.
The public utilities board is investigating a difference between recorded oxygen use and delivered volume.
The eastern floating settlement on {world} has missed its scheduled supply launch. Coastguard traffic is searching the route.
A dispute over offshore anchoring rights has stalled the arrival of three deep-water freighters.
The harbour authority closed the outer docks after a rogue swell damaged their support struts.
A research submersible has surfaced with a damaged sampling arm and no mission data.
The ferry union voted to suspend crossings until emergency raft inspections are completed.
The offshore desalination plant denies reports that its intake filters have collapsed.
Two fishermen rescued an unregistered passenger capsule floating outside the designated shipping lanes.
An underwater construction crew has found an object beneath the foundation piles and stopped work pending identification.
Security advisory for {world} remains amber. Travellers should confirm local conditions with their destination contacts.
A cargo insurer has stopped writing new policies for unsupervised surface deliveries on {world}.
Port police are taking statements after a transport convoy failed to arrive at its scheduled checkpoint.
A passenger ferry was turned back after a navigation beacon transmitted conflicting instructions.
Medical staff have asked for armed escorts between the clinic and the outer settlement. The request is under review.
A security cordon remains in place around the main transmitter. Authorities won't comment on its purpose.
The local council says the port is open. Three independent captains say the approach is not safe.
{world} port authority has revised its after-dark arrival procedures. The advisory is still in force.
A survey crew reports its remote equipment was removed while its camp was unoccupied.
The planetary administration disputes a merchant association report of repeated cargo thefts.
The missing convoy has been found. Officials have not released the condition of the drivers.
A visiting diplomat has cancelled public appearances. The port has not changed its arrival schedule.
The station administrator says the security operation has ended. Patrol craft remain in position.
Travellers are being asked not to accept navigation services from unregistered traffic in the outer approach.
An investigation into fraudulent landing clearances is ongoing. Valid permits can still be verified directly with control.
Advisory remains red for {world}. The port's last published status has not been independently confirmed.
A courier arriving from {world} delivered an undated evacuation order. Officials are checking its authenticity.

The town clinic is accepting walk-ins. Outsiders must bring identification and a payment method.
Cargo storage available by the week. We have a lock and we use it.
Books traded, repaired, and copied at Low Door Press. Bring something worth reading.
Visit the market behind the municipal hall. Not the one behind the old municipal hall.
Three day excursion to the northern survey camp. You carry your own air, we carry the maps.
Local driver available for your next delivery. Passenger rates and freight rates are not the same.
Employment board at {world}: watchkeepers, mechanics, two people who can keep a secret about a wedding.
The Pilgrim's Cup. Breakfast all shifts. Bring your own argument; we have enough of ours.
East Canal Apartments: private berths for crew staying a month or more. Short-term inquiries politely declined.
We don't sell the cheapest drive parts. We sell the ones that passed inspection.
Make port and lose your bag? Visit the property office before buying everything again.
{world} public transit announces new shuttle routes to the freight yards. Changes effective immediately.
The crew registry has openings for qualified pilots. No, 'qualified' does not mean 'owns a jacket.'
Need a berth with privacy? Ask for Deck Four Lodge. Need privacy from customs? Do not ask for Deck Four Lodge.
The municipal archives will certify your birth records for a fee. Forgeries reported to the authorities.
{world} transit network apologises for yesterday. Today's service is running on yesterday's schedule.
The Constellation Theatre presents 'The Last Jump' on the lower concourse. No refunds for technical inaccuracies.
Overnight secure storage for freight and personal effects. We are not responsible for personal grudges.
Need to hire a thousand temporary workers? Staffing Hall has three thousand applicants and two functioning counters.
The Inner Ring Noodle Shop. Don't call ahead. By the time you arrive, it'll be a different table.
Industrial claims bureau. One appointment, fourteen signatures, fewer surprises than your insurer.
{world} surface shuttles: reserved seating for families, military transfers, and anyone willing to pay for it.
New arrivals housing cooperative. Two-year waiting list; earlier openings possible if someone leaves the planet.
Naval-base family housing board on {world}. Civilian contractors welcome to apply, subject to the usual checks.
Fleet surplus auction. Lots inspected by appointment. Neither operational status nor good sense guaranteed.
Veterans' dining hall outside the base gate. Uniform not required; stories optional.
Scout Service mess at {world} is looking for a civilian cook. Must tolerate uncertain schedules.
Survey charts repaired and copied outside the base. Originals remain with their owners.
Retired Scout? Know where to find a good mechanic? The survey club meets on rest-day.
Survey watch accommodation near {world}. Weekly rates for visiting crews. Very quiet when the scouts are gone.
Navigation instruments calibrated in the old stores hut. Ask for the technician, not the duty watch.
Former scout field kits available. Inventory may contain personal letters; please return them.
Contractor lodging near {world} base. Pass checks are your responsibility.
Tailor for service uniforms, formal dress, and repairs after unofficial sporting events.
The north-gate canteen is accepting civilian diners again. The entrance has moved.
Courier depot staff sale on {world}: office terminals, broken furniture, and perfectly good locks with no keys.
Secure document transport by appointment. Ask about insurance before handing anything over.
The base-side printer will copy your charts. We reserve the right to ask why you're printing forty.
Depot shift canteen, east gate. We feed workers before their supervisors.
Used cargo restraints by the pallet, inspected, tagged, and reasonably honest about their age.
Depot freight sorting seeks temporary clerks with legible handwriting and no outstanding warrants.
A ship is a home until the air recycler breaks. Haddon Mechanical. We answer calls.
Need someone found? We're investigators, not miracle workers. It matters which one you need.
A quiet night's sleep guaranteed. We guarantee quiet. We do not guarantee sleep.
We buy dead computers. We'll even buy the one that made you think it was alive.
Passenger berths available on the next outward ship. No guarantee of an interesting destination.
Double-check your fuel accounting. A missing litre is a missing litre, even if the purser can't find it.
Clean laundry in six hours. Dirty laundry in four if you help fold.
Repair your vacc suit before you need it. You can test the seals here, and we'll show you the leak.
Fifty years in the cargo business. Thirty of them profitable.
Local legal counsel. Ship mortgages, salvage disputes, divorce across three worlds. We handle the paperwork.
Want to talk to your family? Leave a message with the next outbound packet. No, it isn't instant.
We serve all species at the same counter. We do not serve all species the same food.
Your old ship deserves an honest valuation. What you deserve is between you and the ship.
The doctor has appointments. Emergencies do not need appointments. Misunderstandings do.
Lost your favourite card game? We sell decks with all the cards still in them.
We purchase damaged cargo, including damaged cargo whose owner insists it is not damaged.
The Silent Hour: private dining room, sound isolation, and an owner who won't ask you about the trade deal.
Work gloves in six sizes. Don't ask for seven. You're not the first to ask.
Crew counselling and mediation. Because a week in jump can feel like a month at a table.
You can fix a hull with bad metal. You can also come to us and do it properly.
Foundry seeks someone with experience teaching machines to stop. Pay negotiable.
Bring your own suit. Rent our tools. Save your life. Not necessarily in that order.
The Stone Glass tavern reminds patrons that borrowed money is still money.
For the last time, this is a shipping agency, not a marriage bureau. Unless there are two berths available.
We don't know what you need. That's why our catalogue has twenty thousand entries and a human operator.
Ship's log, {ship}. Day three, I think. The medic and the navigator disagree about whether a day means anything in here.
Bridge recorder. The door from engineering has started sticking. We did not put that in the maintenance report.
{ship} internal. Tell the cook the emergency rations are for an emergency. Not a shortage of onions.
Engineering watch. Jump readings nominal. The vibration is a cabinet latch; I checked it twice.
Captain's personal log. I thought I'd like the quiet. Apparently I do not.
Bridge to mess. I can hear the singing from here. You've been warned.
{ship} stores report: we're short one pressure suit. Nobody knows why and nobody admits borrowing one.
Internal message for the captain: our passenger wants to see the outside view. I've explained there isn't one.
Maintenance note, {ship}. The portside lamp flashes when the galley heater cycles. Either can wait until we emerge.
Ship recorder. Six of us, seven places set for dinner. The cook says that's always happened.
Navigation log. I haven't changed the plotted arrival point. Stop asking me if we're there yet.
Crew bulletin: water recycling has reached the part of its service life where it makes the coffee taste metallic.
Medical log, {ship}. Another passenger reports the same dream. Probably the bad tea.
Bridge log. Had to tell the new deckhand that a week in jump does not mean a week of leave.
{ship} internal. Somebody left a note on the airlock: 'DO NOT OPEN'. This is not helpful information in jump.
Captain to engineering: if that's a joke, I'm writing you up. If it isn't, come to the bridge.
Galley log. The Vargr passenger says the table seating is an insult. Nobody will tell me whom we've insulted.
Internal crew broadcast. The cards are marked, all the cards, so if you want to cheat find another game.
Ship's log. No contact with normal space, as expected. I keep checking anyway.
Engineering to bridge. A faint noise in the jump drive cabinet. It stops when someone opens it.
{ship} internal. Doctor says the passenger's hearing is fine. That doesn't explain the voice he says he hears.
Crew message to the purser: I know the passenger's name is on the list. I'm asking whose cabin he's in.
Private recording. I used to hate the noise of the manoeuvre drive. I would like to hear it now.
Bridge note. Zero outbound transmissions possible. The student keeps trying to send one home.
Mess announcement: whoever replaced the coffee with a nutritionally equivalent beverage can replace it back.
{ship} to traffic, emerged from jump and acquiring local navigation. We have an arrival report to file.
Approach control, {ship}. Requesting current port conditions. Our packet's a week old.
{ship} to any traffic ahead. We're decelerating with a damaged thruster. Give us room to turn.
{ship} here. Does the outer marker still exist or are we looking at somebody's abandoned beacon?
Captain to control. We can take a hold. We cannot take a day. Fuel is the priority.
{ship} inbound from the jump limit. One passenger needs medical attention on arrival.
{ship}, transmitting on common. We are attempting to identify a nonresponsive object on our track.
{ship} to port traffic, requesting docking after a jump. Our cargo seals are intact. Our catering is not.
We have a navigation chart marked with three stations. I see two. Which one did you lose?
{ship} to ground. We're carrying a coffin. Please tell us whether the family has been contacted.
This is {ship}. The distress signal you relayed? We found its transmitter. There's no ship.
{ship}, port control. Sorry, wrong channel. If anybody heard a request for replacement filters, it's still a request.
Approach, our ship's clock and the port's bulletin disagree. State current local time, please.
{ship}, passing the hundred-diameter line inbound. Permission to alter vector toward the highport?
{ship} to the lighter off our bow. Your cargo door is open. Are you aware?
Control, you have our crew count. It changed during jump. We need to speak to someone privately.
{ship}, inbound. We picked up a navigation buoy broadcasting an invalid date. Can you confirm the current chart issue?
Port authority, we have unrefined fuel aboard. Request facilities before loading refined stores.
Approach, be advised the local patrol has been following us since emergence. We would appreciate an explanation.
This is {ship}. We're not on your traffic list because we weren't expected to come back.
{ship} to skimming traffic off {gasGiant}. Making one pass and climbing. Do not cross our ascent.
Gas giant approach, this is {ship}. We have a storm cell larger than the charted zone.
{ship}, holding off {gasGiant}. The fuel scoop is binding. Engineering wants another pass; command doesn't.
Skimmer on the lee side, your drive wash is interfering with our collector. Back off.
{ship} to anyone in the upper atmosphere of {gasGiant}: we have a blind spot in our aft sensors.
Fuel scoop temperatures are rising. {ship} aborting skim. Clear our escape vector.
{ship} here. We think that ribbon ahead is ring debris, not cloud. Anyone have a better return?
Stand by, control. We are not climbing through that cell just to make your appointment.
{gasGiant} skimming group, copy our telemetry. Did you see that pressure spike too?
{ship}, out of the atmosphere and checking fuel contamination. We're not committing to jump yet.
Unidentified craft below our orbit, this is {ship}. We are not looking for trouble. We are looking for clear space.
{ship} to the refuel barge. You've got a flexible line drifting free. It is moving toward us.
We've lost the scoop door actuator on {ship}. We can retract manually. We need someone to stay off the starboard side.
To the ship that skimmed before us: thanks for telling us the upper layer was quiet. It wasn't.
Aboard {ship}, fuel transfer interrupted. Water in the collection line; confirming source.
{ship} off {gasGiant}. We'd appreciate weather radar from anyone whose sensors aren't currently full of hydrogen.
This is the third pass we have not taken. We will wait for better conditions.
Our pilot says the cloud tower isn't rising. Our instruments say otherwise. We are leaving.
{ship} to nearby traffic: the ring plane is more crowded than the published chart indicates.
Refuel ship to the free trader below. Your fuel doors are still open. Check them before ascent.
{ship} working {belt}. If you're the cutter on our port quarter, your transponder's wrong.
Prospector on {belt}, this is {ship}. We are not taking your claim. We are crossing your vector.
{ship} to any salvage tugs: we have a loose freight module, slow tumble, no identifiable owner.
The rock moved. The rock wasn't supposed to move. {ship} requesting survey traffic.
{ship} to {belt} miners. Who's drilling without a warning charge? Our survey plates are vibrating.
We have a thermal bloom beneath the debris. Could be equipment, could be somebody's camp.
{ship} here. We lost our lidar for six seconds. If anybody saw the object crossing our nose, please call.
Our cutter has an injured operator. Transferring him to {ship}; keep the lane clear.
To the green-hulled freighter, that ore body belongs to us. The beacon did not fall off by itself.
{ship}, stationkeeping by the outer claim marker. The marker has been cut free and moved.
I can see your mining laser, captain. No, it isn't pointed away from traffic.
{belt} patrol, this is {ship}. We're reporting a vessel with no running lights inside an active work zone.
Our cargo container ruptured on loading. Loose ore drifting near the service track.
The nav solution's good. The debris map isn't. Those are different things.
{ship} to the drill crew: stop the charge sequence. Our tug is still alongside the rock.
Mining tender to all traffic: explosive separation in thirty seconds. Don't ask if it's close; check the coordinates.
This is {ship}. We found your survey drone. It's following a ship that left an hour ago.
Anyone operating in {belt} running an old mass driver? We're seeing impacts without a corresponding signal.
{ship} to support. Need a tow on one small workboat. Batteries drained, pilot deeply annoyed.
{belt} control, if there is one: our claims map has overlapping rights. We won't cut until that's resolved.
{ship} to {ship2}, your aft hatch is venting. If that's planned, you have unusual plans.
{ship} to passing traffic. Does anybody have an updated local chart? The one we bought is fiction.
Copy your hail. We're having trouble with the translator. Give me the numbers slowly.
This is {ship}, looking for a medic. Human, Vargr, anyone with training. Passenger's in a bad way.
{ship} to port, we're late because the manoeuvre drive isn't happy. Neither is engineering.
Whoever's transmitting music on emergency, congratulations, we can all hear your music.
{ship}, standing by to transfer passengers. Tell your purser we've got no room for their luggage.
Control, please repeat the docking fee. My first officer has fallen out of his chair.
{ship} to the vessel marked private. Your collision lights are out. Privacy won't protect the hull.
We're sending the data by narrow beam. Stop asking us to read forty pages aloud.
This is {ship}. Passenger manifest says eight. We're counting nine. Calling port security.
{ship} to the tanker ahead: are those warning buoys yours? They weren't there yesterday.
Negative, I won't repeat that on an open channel. Put a supervisor on.
{ship}, requesting a pilot with experience in low-visibility approach. We can pay, within reason.
Calling the owner of a red cargo sled. It's attached to the underside of our ship. We did not authorise that.
Port authority, {ship}. Our transponder was replaced after a fire. The old registration is still being broadcast by something else.
To the crewman waving from the service gantry: we're on a different station. You have the wrong freighter.
{ship}, leaving the berth. If the crate's still aboard, consider it delivered somewhere else.
I have your docking solution. I don't have a tug, and I don't have confidence in the other one.
Unidentified patrol vessel, we can see your weapons ports. You can stop pretending this is an equipment check.
{ship} to {ship2}, we heard your mayday call. You didn't send one? Then we've got a problem.
To the station mechanic: the ship's air smells wrong after your last repair. Come smell it yourself.
{ship} to convoy lead, one of your tankers is falling behind. Do you want us to call them or you?
You can cut my speed or you can cut my cargo. Pick one.
{ship} to local authority. We're carrying wounded civilians and we need somewhere to put them down.
This is {ship}. We will accept your conditions, but the agreement is with the crew, not the vessel.
We are neither your quarry nor your escort. You have placed yourself in our path. Correct this.
The word you translated as 'captain' is a plural. There are three decision-makers aboard. Please be patient.
Your boarding request has been received by the elder. The elder is sleeping. We will not wake them for customs.
We counted five human voices in your last transmission. Your registry says four crew. Is one of you being transported as cargo?
Our name is not what your machine says. Use the hull number until we can agree on sounds.
We have no individual who speaks for all of us. State your demand and it will be distributed.
Your offer of a single berth for our kin group is inappropriate. We accept your apology before you make it.
There are twelve minutes between your words and ours. Do not interpret the delay as disagreement.
We do not understand why you call this ship female. The ship has not expressed a sex.
The pack leader is not the oldest voice. You have offended the oldest voice by assuming it was.
We would prefer you not use the word 'purchase' for living organisms, even those you call food.
{ship} to traffic. Our ship has no exterior markings visible in your spectrum. We are still there.
We're not pirates. Pirates would ask you to stop. We're asking you to move.
{ship}, ending transmission. Engineering has just handed me a worse problem.
A naval clerk bought civilian clothes for six officers yesterday. All the same size, all paid in cash.
The hospital got a call from the base to prepare a ward. Nobody came through the front door.
That patrol cruiser came home under tow. The press photograph somehow doesn't show the damage.
An officer I trust says the missing gunner was never assigned to that ship. His sister has the service letters.
They've asked the fuel yard for double the usual storage and half the usual paperwork.
A dockworker found a child's drawing inside a sealed military container. Don't know what to make of it.
The base watch changed its call signs three times last night. That's usually paperwork, except nobody warned the tower.
The scout who came back wouldn't let them touch his astrogation computer. He carried it into the medical wing himself.
There's a survey map on the mess wall with one system scratched out. New recruits keep asking why.
Two couriers went out with the same sealed packet. They didn't tell either pilot there was another.
That old scout has slept at the base every night since her ship vanished. Doesn't own a room anywhere else.
The Service paid for an entire fuel tank and burned none of it. Somebody signed for the transfer anyway.
A cartographer quit after the third correction to the same set of coordinates.
The waystation logged a ship arriving before its own departure notice. Likely a clock error. The clocks checked out.
A scout brought back a box of empty sample vials. Refused to say what he found.
The last survey team sent its map corrections privately, not over the normal route.
The station storekeeper keeps ordering children's medical supplies. There are no families assigned there.
They've changed the guard over the old survey antenna, but no one will admit it's still in service.
Somebody's moving ammunition through the civilian stores because the official inventory is too visible.
One of the garrison officers has two names and no one agrees which one is real.
They dug a second gate in the base wall, then covered it with fresh concrete.
The base commander has been seen at the port in civilian clothes, meeting the same ship every month.
The men guarding the northern depot don't wear the local unit insignia.
The communications office paid to have an old relay repaired, then told technicians to leave it powered off.
Two identical outgoing packets were given different priority seals.
The night operator resigned without clearing her desk. Someone else collected her things before dawn.
They're routing some mail through a ship that isn't on the courier schedule.
A clerk says the station is keeping a copy of every deleted message. I don't know who'd want that job.
The depot received four sealed crates, opened one, and sent the other three back without recording them.
A supply sergeant has been buying old vacc suits with cash. A lot of old vacc suits.
Three transport crews say they've hauled the same container on different dates. None were allowed to open it.
An empty barracks has been drawing food rations for months.
The depot is paying for repairs to a ship that doesn't appear on its inventory.
Somebody has been replacing old claim beacons around {belt} with perfectly new ones. Every registered owner denies it.
The miners swear the ore cutter that vanished last season is still being billed for fuel.
A prospector found fresh welding on a derelict that has been tumbling for forty years.
The old survey charts show a rock where the current charts show empty space. The rock is too large to miss.
A crew in {belt} came back with new pressure suits, new credits, and no ore.
There's a salvage tug out there hauling containers with the ownership tags sanded off.
Nobody takes the direct approach through the central rocks any more. Nobody will tell me what happened.
The prospectors say a ship is running dark near the claim line. The authorities say it's a sensor ghost.
An entire mining crew demanded separate passage offworld. They wouldn't share a compartment with each other.
A surveyor says the old listening post is still broadcasting something into the belt. Very low power.
They say the new ore body has structural ribs in it. I don't want to hear what that means.
The cutters leave {belt} by different routes every time, even when they're carrying nothing.
One miner offered half his claim to anyone who'd come back and tow his equipment. Nobody took it.
The assay lab rejected the sample because the elements weren't distributed like natural rock.
Somebody has marked a path through the belt with emergency beacons. None are reporting emergencies.
{world}'s port manager retired on a pension she couldn't have earned in three lifetimes. Officially, she was lucky with investments.
A customs clerk found the same ship name on three arrival lists. Different hull numbers.
Somebody's been paying to keep an empty storage locker powered and cooled for eleven years.
The quietest family in town keeps importing industrial air filters for a house with no machinery.
The old museum exhibits went into storage. What's on display now are very good copies.
Two ships left {world} on the same day and separately warned us not to refuel at the east depot.
The constable who signed the search warrant is reportedly missing. The warrant has not been withdrawn.
Every transport company on {world} has the same unmarked detour on its route sheet.
A mechanic said the patrol wanted a particular passenger, not the ship. That would explain the damage.
The warning beacon is broadcasting from a different position each night.
The colonel says the road is safe. The road crews keep finding fresh shell fragments.
That last ship from {world} had every window covered from the inside.
A courier got paid to carry a message to {world}. He brought it back unopened, along with a refund.
The official port frequency still plays the same weather bulletin. Dates included. It's months old.
They say the government evacuated its own families before they posted the red notice.
A ship sold its entire cargo cheap to avoid another approach. It had spent a week waiting for clearance.
The local traffic controller changed voice halfway through a transmission and never acknowledged the handover.
A woman on {world} claims to own the landing field because she repaired it last year. Nobody has proven her wrong.
There are three different tax collectors working the port. All three insist the others are criminals.
The settlement hired its own constable after the last one declared independence.
Two villages are paying each other for the same water pipeline. No one remembers who built it.
The town council meets in a ship because nobody agrees which building counts as town hall.
The company on {world} has been buying its own shares through a freight subsidiary.
A supervisor who was supposed to be transferred six months ago still has a badge that opens every door.
The last labour settlement included a clause neither side will publicly explain.
The company store has two price lists. One for workers and one for visitors with cameras.
Someone bought the rights to the drinking water and then stopped billing for it. That's what scares people.
The ship came out of jump with two more hours on the clocks than on the crew logs. They made everyone sign the clocks were wrong.
I know a purser who keeps a second passenger list. She calls it the list of people who actually arrived.
A courier dropped a sealed envelope at the port office. They sent a guard to burn the letter, not read it.
That freighter has had four captains in a year. It's the same crew in every photograph.
Somebody bought up every vacancy on the next two outbound passenger ships. They haven't used a single seat.
A woman in the clinic pays strangers to take pictures of the sky. Same time every night.
The old sensor station is still drawing power. Not much, but enough to keep something awake.
They said the cargo was ceremonial. Ceremonial cargo doesn't usually need a cold-storage unit.
The captain who reported the derelict refuses to collect the salvage fee. Wants the report withdrawn.
There's a ship in drydock that no one remembers bringing in. The work order is paid in full.
My cousin works in the registrar's office. Three people with the same face filed for separate birth certificates.
The customs computer recognised a dead man as he walked through the gate. The officer let him go.
I was offered a job moving a crate from one warehouse to the next. Paid more than a year's wages. I declined.
The last trader left her fuel behind and jumped on reserve. Didn't even unload the cargo.
Someone has been replacing the town's public safety notices with exact copies. Only the dates change.
The hospital's missing a whole shift on the roster. Their pay keeps going to valid accounts.
A Vargr engineer bought a human wedding ring and had it machined to fit an airlock handle. Wouldn't say why.
A spacer says the distress beacon was transmitting before the ship was built. That sounds like a paperwork problem to me.
One of the station's oldest maintenance corridors has been sealed from the wrong side.
They found cargo from the wreck in a shop three days before they found the wreck.
An Aslan trader took a loss rather than accept a berth named after someone else's ancestor.
That quiet old man at the canteen used to give Navy officers orders. I've seen them stand when he enters.
The station's holovid camera has a blind spot exactly where the auctioneer meets his customers.
A family has spent twenty years waiting for a ship the port records say never departed.
The pawn broker has a dozen identical wristwatches. All stopped on different days at the same time.
A trader says he delivered medicine to a town on a dead world. The address paid in advance.
Somebody keeps making offers on that abandoned ship. They only bid when a crew member dies.
The archivist says last year's port register was destroyed in a flood. The archive's in orbit.
They never opened the coffin. The quarantine officer signed the release after talking to somebody on a private channel.
One of the shuttle pilots won't fly over the old prison. He's happy to fly anywhere else.
Every ship that visits the new refuelling station leaves with a full tank and a different navigator.
A Hiver offered to purchase my debts. Not pay them. Purchase them, including the people who owe me.
I met a man who insisted he was my great-grandson. He knew the name of my first ship. I'm not that old.
The priest on the next dock was asking the computer to translate a language it had never heard. Nobody else could hear him speaking.
A merchant's insurance paid out for a ship that later came back. Nobody's asked for the money back.
The new security officer checked the camera logs and asked to be removed from every photograph.
They say the admiral has a second crew, not a second ship. Only ever flies with one at a time.
The port keeps a berth empty on the first day of every month. Never gives a reason. Nobody books it now.
I went to deliver the parcel and the recipient gave me a photograph of me delivering it.
The man who owns the free trader also owns the debt on half the ships docked here. That's why he doesn't fly.
The last time I saw that cargo seal it was on a museum case. Now it's on a refrigerated container.
I heard a voice from a powered-down bridge speaker. Could be induction. I wish they'd stop repeating the coordinates.
They're not looking for the cargo. They're looking for whoever can open it.
The customs official apologised to the smuggler. In front of witnesses. Then waved the ship through.
The engineer says the reactor never went critical. The scorch marks say he isn't telling the whole story.
Their entire passenger list reads as one family. Their names don't share a language.
People here say the old colony ship is still overhead, above the tracking limit. I haven't seen it.
The ship's surgeon put an emergency call to a doctor who died last year. Someone answered.
Two buyers separately asked me for the same anonymous passenger list. Neither cared what it cost.
Nobody can name the first person to settle here. Every record begins with the second.
Mayday, mayday, this is a container lighter in the {port} cargo approach. We've lost attitude control. Unable to arrest tumble.
{port} rescue relay: pressure loss reported aboard incoming freighter. Medical and salvage craft requested.
Emergency traffic: docking arm failed under load. Two workers outside the pressure shell. Repeat, two workers outside.
This is {ship}, cargo corridor. Fire in the forward equipment bay. Our suppression system is offline.
{port} control, ship in berth four reports trapped personnel behind a jammed pressure door. Rescue team en route.
Mayday, {port}. Small craft disabled beyond the outer marker. Three aboard. Battery reserve declining.
{ship} declaring emergency. We cannot close the fuel manifold. Request a clear berth, no ignition sources nearby.
{port} tower relaying a medical evacuation request from a vessel with life-support failure.
Emergency frequency, survey shuttle on approach. Pilot unresponsive. Automatic landing system not engaged.
Help required. We've struck an uncharted object. Hull is holding, reactor scram complete, crew count uncertain.
{port}, this is {ship}. Gear failure, descending. We need the emergency vehicles at the south end.
Mayday. Fire on the lower cargo deck. Smoke entering the passenger section. We are turning back.
{port} field, medical priority inbound. Passenger is not breathing without assistance.
Calling all local craft. Tug has separated from freighter under load. Cable is free and moving.
{ship} to ground. We're on the pad, but the ramp is jammed and the atmosphere alarms are sounding.
Emergency call to {port}. We have a crewman outside with a damaged suit. Request a recovery vehicle now.
{ship} losing altitude over the western approach. Manoeuvre control intermittent. Clear the landing area.
Mayday, mayday. Vehicle overturned outside the field. Life-support bottles almost empty.
To anyone at {port}, the fuel shed is burning. We are moving away from the tanks.
This is the clinic at {port}. We need a medical shuttle. The road is cut off.
Mayday near {port}. We're losing power and we cannot see the landing marker. Anybody on the ground, answer.
{ship} on emergency. One engine is locked full thrust. We are moving away from the settlement.
To the field at {port}: emergency landing imminent. Nobody on the strip, please. Nobody.
Anybody listening near {port}, we have a casualty and a broken ambulance. We need a ship's medic.
This is the freighter outside {port}. We're out of fuel, out of power, and the air is getting warm.
Someone please reply. We can hear the beacon but we can't get a signal back.
Mayday over {world}. No tower answering. We've put down hard and the forward hull is open.
Automated distress transmission: emergency battery active, crew status unknown, origin {world} surface.
This is {ship}, over {world}. Our lander has missed the retrieval window. Searching last known position.
Mayday. Survey team missing after surface traverse. We have one working vehicle and no daylight plan.
Anyone in orbit of {world}, confirm receipt. We have injured personnel and no surface transport.
This is the last portable transmitter we have. Please mark our coordinates when the signal stops.
Mayday near {gasGiant}. Fuel-skimming craft has lost thrust control. We are descending below planned altitude.
{ship} to all traffic above {gasGiant}. Scoop door jammed open. We cannot hold our ascent profile.
Distress traffic. One person overboard from the collection platform. Suit beacon active, closing fast on atmosphere.
Mayday. Refuelling vessel vented contaminated hydrogen into the drive bay. Reactor shut down. We need a tow.
We are losing the pressure boundary in the forward tanks. Repeat, forward tanks. Breaking off skim now.
